exposure: previous major traumas (traumatic brain injury, spine fracture, pelvic fracture, hip or thigh fracture)
cohort: The study included 18,573 pregnancies of women who experienced major traumas before pregnancy, compared to a control group of individuals with wrist fractures.
finding: The study found no evidence of differences in maternal fear of childbirth in patients with preceding major traumas when compared to a control group, concluding that the major trauma itself is likely the explanatory factor for an increased rate of elective cesarean birth.
mod_finding: Among women diagnosed with fear of childbirth, those with previous spine fractures had the highest adjusted odds for elective cesarean birth as an intended mode of delivery (aOR 2.28) compared to the control group.
